label: Reprieve, not relief
summary: The world edges up to 44, still firmly in the 'Mixed / uneasy' band, on the strength of one large piece of good news that arrived overnight. President Trump announced on Truth Social late Saturday that he had cancelled the planned bombing campaign against Iran's energy infrastructure — the strikes CBS and the Wall Street Journal reported were being prepared for this weekend — saying Iran and other regional governments had asked him to hold off and that 'the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to,' including the 'Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT' and an end to Iran's nuclear threat. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is reported to have called Trump urging exactly that, and Israel agreed to join the commitment. The caveats are heavy: Tehran issued no confirmation, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned of a 'proportionate response' to any attack, the State Department kept security alerts running for Americans in ten countries, and almost no terms have been published. The reprieve is real but unratified, and the rest of the ledger stayed dark. Israeli forces killed eight Palestinians across Gaza on Sunday, two days after the Board of Peace published its 15-point disarmament-and-withdrawal roadmap, with Hamas saying it will hand over weapons only after Israel halts operations and withdraws, and an Israeli official saying there will be no withdrawal without 'genuine disarmament.' Russia's second mass attack on Kyiv in 48 hours — 35 missiles and 185 drones — killed at least nine and injured more than twenty; Zelensky said only one of 27 ballistic missiles was intercepted because there are no Patriot interceptors left. A homemade bomb killed three outside a central Moscow restaurant. Europe's slow-motion climate emergency reached a milestone: Hungary shut the Paks nuclear plant completely for the first time since 1982 because the Danube has fallen toward minus 144 centimetres and can no longer cool it, taking out nearly half the country's electricity, with Prime Minister Peter Magyar warning of an energy crisis as soon as Monday and Romania closing reactors for the same reason. Spain put the Ceuta death toll at 67 after 50,000 to 60,000 people breached the enclave's frontier. A sightseeing flight over Peru's Nazca Lines crashed and killed 13, eleven of them Italian, German and Spanish tourists. Rescuers recovered the body of Nirmal Purja, one of ten climbers killed by an avalanche on Broad Peak. Oil closed July up about 24 percent, with Brent at 90.17 dollars, a cost-of-living hit that the Sunday announcement may begin to unwind. Against that: Virunga National Park has stood up six health checkpoints, 40 paramedics and 80 rangers to hold back an Ebola epidemic that has now killed more than 1,400 people in eastern DRC; the Glasgow Commonwealth Games closed at the OVO Hydro with the largest para-sport programme in the Games' history and a handover to Ahmedabad 2030; and NASA's Curiosity rover reported a valley-wide field of honeycomb polygons on Mars pointing to a past environment that could have supported life. The headline matches the rubric formula with no editorial adjustment.

drivers.headline: Trump cancels the planned large-scale strike on Iran's energy infrastructure, posting late Saturday that Iran and other Middle Eastern countries asked him to hold off and that 'the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to' — a deal he says would bring the 'Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT' and end Iran's nuclear threat, with Israel agreeing to join the commitment and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman reported to have telephoned urging a return to negotiations; Tehran gave no immediate confirmation, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned any US or Israeli attack would draw a 'proportionate response,' and the State Department kept security alerts in place for Americans in ten regional countries

Israeli forces kill at least eight Palestinians across Gaza on Sunday — including a man and a woman hit by a helicopter strike on an apartment south of Deir el-Balah, three in Khan Younis and one in Gaza City's Old City — two days after the Board of Peace published its 15-point roadmap for Hamas disarmament and Israeli withdrawal; Hamas says it will hand its weapons over for storage only once Israel halts operations and withdraws under last year's agreement, while an Israeli official told Reuters there will be no withdrawal from current positions without 'genuine disarmament'

Russia hits Kyiv with 35 missiles and 185 attack drones in its second mass attack on Ukraine in 48 hours, killing at least nine people and injuring more than twenty including four children; Ukrainian air defences shot down 154 drones but only one of 27 ballistic missiles, which Zelensky attributed bluntly to having no interceptors left for the Patriot system, and Mayor Vitali Klitschko called it 'a horrific night for Kyiv'

A homemade bomb detonates at about 8:10pm outside the Balzi Rossi restaurant on Moscow's Kudrinskaya Square during a private event, killing a security guard who stopped the woman carrying the device, a customer, and the woman herself, and injuring more than twenty others; Russian authorities have not identified her or stated a motive, and it is unclear whether the device was detonated deliberately

Hungary shuts down the Paks nuclear power plant completely for the first time since it opened in 1982 because record-low Danube water levels leave it without enough cooling water, with output falling from a normal 2,000 megawatts to 240 overnight before the final reactor powered down; the river is expected to reach minus 144 centimetres against a previous 2018 record of minus 98, the plant supplies nearly half of Hungary's electricity, more than 100 towns and villages are under water-use restrictions, Romania has closed reactors for the same reason, and Prime Minister Peter Magyar warned an energy crisis could begin as early as Monday

Spain's government puts the death toll from the Ceuta border crisis at 67 — some drowned, some killed in a stampede across a breakwater barrier — after between 50,000 and 60,000 people breached the frontier of the small Spanish territory in North Africa between Thursday and Friday; Madrid is installing a 500-metre containment barrier along the breakwater into the sea, the interior ministry says most of those who crossed have already returned to Morocco, and some of those still in Ceuta say shops have been closed to force them back

Oil closes out July with a monthly gain of roughly 24 percent — Brent at 90.17 dollars and WTI at 85.94 after Friday's session — as Iran's Revolutionary Guards stopped two tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz and four others changed course, leaving traffic through the waterway thin on Kpler tracking data even though two very large crude carriers did exit the Gulf; the war premium is a direct cost-of-living tax worldwide, and whether Sunday's cancellation of the US strike unwinds it will not be visible until markets reopen

A small Aerodiana aircraft carrying tourists on a sightseeing flight over Peru's Nazca Lines crashes in the Pueblo Viejo area roughly four miles from the city of Nazca, killing all 13 on board — 11 foreign tourists, described by Peru's transport ministry as Italian, German and Spanish, and two crew — after taking off from Pisco airport

Pakistani rescuers recover the body of Nirmal Purja, the Nepali-born former British soldier who climbed all fourteen 8,000-metre peaks in a record 189 days, one of ten climbers killed when an avalanche swept the main west gully of Broad Peak in the Karakoram; the dead include Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy of Oman, Pur Bahadur Gurung of Nepal, Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi and climbers from China and the United States

Virunga National Park, Africa's oldest, mounts an emergency response to keep the DR Congo Ebola epidemic out of both its surrounding communities and its endangered mountain gorillas, establishing six health checkpoints along a 300km stretch of protected forest across North Kivu and deploying 40 paramedics alongside 80 rangers for an initial six months; director Emmanuel de Merode argues the uninhabited forest itself acts as a barrier to transmission, as it did during the 2018-2020 outbreak, in a country's 17th outbreak that has now killed more than 1,400 people

The Glasgow Commonwealth Games close at the OVO Hydro on Sunday evening with Simple Minds, Delta Goodrem and a handover to Amdavad 2030, ending an eleven-day, 74-nation, 2,729-athlete meet that carried the largest para-sport programme in the Games' history at 47 finals, saw women race the mile for the first time, and delivered Rwanda its first ever Commonwealth Games medal; Australia topped the table with 65 golds ahead of England on 26 and Canada on 18, with host Scotland taking 13

NASA's Curiosity rover reports a valley-wide field of honeycomb textures on Mars — polygonal fractures each about 4 to 8 centimetres across, spreading in every direction across the 'Valle Grande' valley in a 360-degree panorama taken on 19 and 20 June — far larger than any patch the mission has found before; the polygons point to repeated wetting and drying, thermal cycling or compaction in sedimentary rock, and together with earlier detections of water-related minerals and organic molecules they strengthen the case that the site once hosted an environment capable of supporting microbial life
